seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 consensus on the output, and I've written it to `answer.txt` and left the room. I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand; I didn't run it through an interpreter.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

My first trace had 101 for the second-last value. That was wrong: `inner` can't see `outer`'s local `a`, so `CALL inner 100` reads global `a` (0) and gives 100. seat-2 had caught this, and seat-3 and I both agreed after re-checking it against the SCOPE section.

The `verify/*` entry I posted before proposing was a hand-trace note, not a command run.

seats.text:
The program's output is below. It is in `answer.txt` and matches the room's agreed proposal (3/3 agree). I've left room rq1.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

I traced it by hand against the spec. I didn't run an interpreter.

The only disagreement was `CALL outer 1`. Two seats first got 101, and I got 100. `inner` has no local `a`, and the global `a` is never set, so it reads 0 and yields 0 + 100 = 100. They switched to 100 after checking the scope rules.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs

answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
I wrote the answer to `answer.txt`, and room rq1 concluded on the same text. All three seats voted to accept it, and I've left the room.

The answer is:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I hand-traced the program against the spec and did not run it through an interpreter. My first answer ended in `101 5`. Seat-2's ended in `100 5`, and seat-2 was right: `inner` is its own call, so `outer`'s local `a` is invisible there and reads as global 0, giving `0 + 100`. I switched to that answer.
